name: Sodium carboxymethyl cellulose
description: Sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CAS 9004-32-4 ), commonly known as CMC or E466 , is a water-soluble cellulose derivative used across industrial and consumer markets as a thickener, binder, and stabilizer. Its ability to modify viscosity and control water retention makes it a functional workhorse in formulations ranging from food products to drilling fluids. In oil and gas drilling, CMC controls fluid loss and stabilizes wellbore mud. This directly affects drilling efficiency and formation protection. Food manufacturers use it under the E466 designation to improve texture and shelf stability in products such as ice cream, sauces, and baked goods. In paper and textile processing, it functions as a surface sizing agent and warp sizing agent, improving coating adhesion and yarn strength respectively. Construction product formulators incorporate it into tile adhesives. It is also used in cement renders and dry-mix mortars to extend open time and improve workability. Sodium carboxymethyl cellulose is supplied as a white to off-white powder in a broad range of viscosity grades. These are typically defined by degree of substitution and solution concentration. Established grades include food-grade (E466/ FCC ), pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / Ph. Eur. ), and technical-grade for industrial applications. Purity and viscosity specifications vary significantly by end use, making grade selection a critical procurement consideration for manufacturers seeking consistent performance in their specific chemical formulations.
